verdict.rationale: Buzz exposes its core surfaces programmatically. It is a NIP-29 Nostr relay that third-party clients can connect to directly, which the docs describe as giving API parity through the protocol itself. The official CLI covers channels, repos and branch protection, workflows and approvals, GIFs and more, and the agent skill spans messaging, DMs, users, workflows, feed, reactions, canvas, repos, uploads and memory. Agents are described as able to open repos, send patches, review code, run workflows, edit canvases, create channels and join huddles, and admin, git and agent-identity flows are also API- or key-driven. However, agent creation via CLI only produces a draft that must be finalized in the Desktop UI, and no OpenAPI spec or llms.txt was found. Missing for 10: an explicit documented UI/API parity guarantee or coverage matrix, a machine-readable REST/OpenAPI spec (probes 404), headless finalization of agent creation (currently gated on Desktop review), and independent hands-on corroboration of parity.
